name: Black nail polish for men

lead: Black nail polish for men is a cosmetic coat applied to the fingernails to give a dark, uniform finish. It is part of alternative styles such as goth, punk and rock, and has been marketed to men more openly during the 2020s nail-art boom.
The appearance payoff is a deliberate styling accent that draws attention to well-groomed hands. No studies examine how it affects perceived attractiveness.

paras: It is brushed on as one or two coats on clean, shaped nails, often with a clear top coat, and removed with polish remover. It lasts days rather than weeks and is reapplied as chips appear.
Minor: nail dryness or staining from frequent use and remover, and occasional contact sensitivity to ingredients. Social reception varies by workplace and community.

chain: Dark polish evens nail colour and hides nail imperfections
angle.text: Men use black polish as a styling accent: it makes the nails a uniform dark colour and signals an alt or edgy look. It is temporary and removable.

lead: Nail polish is a lacquer applied to nails, and black is among its oldest colours: sources trace polish to China around 3000 BCE, where red and black later became royal favourites [1]. In the modern West polish has mostly been worn by women, and men wearing it has been seen as breaking traditional gender norms, although its acceptability has shifted with the era [1].

Black polish gives the nails a clean, dark finish that suits alt styles and tidy, groomed hands alike. Its use by men grew visible in the 2020s, when a nail-art boom brought products marketed to men; professional baseball catchers are also noted for wearing polish on the field [1].

paras: Written histories of nail polish trace it to China around 3000 BCE; during the Zhou dynasty royal houses favoured gold and silver, with red and black later replacing them. Ancient Egyptians used henna on nails, and Ming-era polish used beeswax, egg whites, gelatin and vegetable dyes [1]. Modern polishes developed in the 1920s, and painting the whole nail became the norm by the 1940s [1].

In the Western world polish has been worn more by women, and men wearing it can be seen as a departure from traditional gender norms [1]. The 2020s nail-art boom brought polish marketed specifically to men [1].
